full_text_zh:
[P1] 新经典文化
爱心树绘本馆

世界上最大的房子

〔美〕李欧·李奥尼 文·图
阿甲 译

南海出版公司

[P2] 有一群蜗牛住在一棵鲜嫩多汁的卷心菜上。
它们驮着自己的房子，慢悠悠地爬来爬去，
从一片叶子爬到另一片叶子，
寻找最柔嫩的地方来一点一点地啃。

[P3] 有一天，一只小蜗牛对他的爸爸说：
“等我长大了，我要拥有世界上最大的房子。”
“这个想法很愚蠢，”蜗牛爸爸说，“有些东西还是小一点的好。”
这位爸爸是那棵卷心菜上最有智慧的蜗牛，
他为小蜗牛讲了这样一个故事。

从前有一只小蜗牛，就像你一样，
他对他的爸爸说：“等我长大了，
我要拥有世界上最大的房子。”
“有些东西还是小一点的好。”他的爸爸说，
“要让你的房子保持轻巧，才容易驮着走。”

[P4] 可是那只小蜗牛不爱听，
他躲在一片大卷心菜叶的阴影里，扭啊扭、撑啊撑，
各种方法试了又试，终于发现了能让自己的房子长大的方法。

[P5] 房子长啊长啊，卷心菜上的蜗牛们都说：
“你的房子真是世界上最大的房子！”

[P6] 小蜗牛继续扭啊扭、撑啊撑，
直到他的房子大得就像一个瓜。

[P7] 然后，他试着把尾巴快速地拧来拧去，
又学会了怎么让房子长出大大的尖角。

[P8] 他继续挤啊挤、钻啊钻，还拼命地许愿，
终于能够给房子加上
鲜艳的色彩和美丽的图案。

现在，他知道自己的房子是整个世界上
最大的而且是最美丽的房子了。
他很自豪，也很快乐。

[P9] 一群蝴蝶从他的房子上面飞过，
“快看！”一只蝴蝶说，“一座大教堂！”
“不对，”另一只蝴蝶说，“那是马戏团！”
它们绝对想不到，眼前所看到的会是一个蜗牛的房子。

[P10] 还有一家子青蛙，在去远处池塘的路上，忽然停了下来，心中充满了敬畏。
“我的天哪！”它们后来对亲戚们说，
“你们肯定从来没见过那样的奇观——一只普普通通的小蜗牛，
竟然驮着一个像生日蛋糕一样的大房子！”

[P11] 有一天，当蜗牛们吃光了那棵卷心菜上所有的叶子，
只剩下几根疙疙瘩瘩的菜梗时，
它们就要搬到另一棵卷心菜上去了。
可是，天哪，那只小蜗牛根本没法挪动。
他的房子实在是太重了。

[P12] 他只好留了下来，但没有东西可吃，
慢慢地，他变得越来越弱、越来越小。那房子只剩下了空壳。
而那空壳子，也一点一点地，碎了，垮了，
直到最后，什么也没有剩下。

[P13] 故事讲完了。小蜗牛差一点就要哭了。

可是这时候他想起了自己的房子。
“我会让它一直小小的，”他想，
“等我长大了，我想去哪儿就去哪儿。”

[P14] 于是有一天，他轻轻松松、高高兴兴地上路去看世界了。
有些叶子在微风中轻轻摇摆，
有些叶子沉沉地垂向地面。
在黑土地裂开的地方，
水晶在晨曦中闪闪发光。
那边有几个红底圆点的蘑菇，
还有些像塔一样高高耸立的花茎，
顶上的小花仿佛正向人招手。
一颗松果躺在蕨草那像花边一样漂亮的阴影里，
一堆鹅卵石躺在沙床上，光滑圆润，就像斑鸠蛋。
岩石披着苔藓，树木裹着树皮，
柔嫩的花蕾蘸着晨露，芳香清凉。
小蜗牛非常快乐。

[P16] 夏去秋至，冬去春来。
小蜗牛从来也没有忘记爸爸给他讲的故事。
当有人问他：“你的房子怎么会这么小呢？”
他就会说起这个故事——
世界上最大的房子。

full_text_en:
[P1] New Classic Culture
Love Tree Picture Book Library

The Biggest House in the World

[USA] Leo Lionni, Text & Illustrations
Translated by A Jia

Nanhai Publishing Company

[P2] There was a group of snails living on a fresh, juicy cabbage.
They carried their own houses, crawling slowly back and forth,
from one leaf to another,
searching for the tenderest spots to nibble on little by little.

[P3] One day, a little snail said to his dad:
"When I grow up, I want to have the biggest house in the world."
"That idea is silly," said the snail dad, "Some things are better small."
This dad was the wisest snail on the cabbage,
and he told his little snail this story.

Once there was a little snail, just like you,
who said to his dad: "When I grow up,
I want to have the biggest house in the world."
"Some things are better small," his dad said,
"You must keep your house light, so you can carry it easily."

[P4] But that little snail didn't want to listen.
He hid in the shadow of a big cabbage leaf, twisting and stretching,
trying all kinds of methods again and again, until he finally discovered a way to make his house grow bigger.

[P5] The house grew and grew, and the snails on the cabbage all said:
"Your house is truly the biggest house in the world!"

[P6] The little snail kept twisting and stretching,
until his house became as big as a melon.

[P7] Then, he tried quickly twisting his tail back and forth,
and learned how to make his house grow big, sharp points.

[P8] He kept squeezing and drilling, and desperately making wishes,
finally managing to add
bright colors and beautiful patterns to his house.

Now, he knew his house was the biggest and most beautiful house in the whole world.
He was very proud, and very happy.

[P9] A group of butterflies flew over his house.
"Look!" one butterfly said, "A big cathedral!"
"No, no," another butterfly said, "That's a circus!"
They could never have imagined that what they were seeing was a snail's house.

[P10] There was also a family of frogs, on their way to a distant pond, who suddenly stopped, filled with awe.
"Goodness me!" they later told their relatives,
"You've never seen such a sight—just an ordinary little snail,
actually carrying a huge house that looks like a birthday cake!"

[P11] One day, when the snails had eaten all the leaves on that cabbage,
and only a few lumpy, bumpy stalks remained,
they had to move to another cabbage.
But oh dear, that little snail simply couldn't move.
His house was far too heavy.

[P12] He had to stay, but there was nothing to eat.
Slowly, he became weaker and smaller. His house was left as an empty shell.
And that empty shell, bit by bit, broke and collapsed,
until finally, nothing was left.

[P13] The story is over. The little snail was almost going to cry.

But at this moment, he thought of his own house.
"I'll keep it small forever," he thought,
"When I grow up, I can go wherever I want to go."

[P14] One day, he set off to see the world, feeling light and happy.
Some leaves swayed gently in the breeze,
while others drooped heavily toward the ground.
Where the dark earth cracked open,
crystals sparkled in the morning light.
There were a few mushrooms with red caps and white spots,
and some flower stems tall and tower-like,
with tiny blossoms at the top waving as if greeting people.
A pinecone lay in the ferns' shadow, as pretty as lace,
and a pile of smooth, round pebbles rested on the sand, like turtledoves' eggs.
Rocks wore moss, trees wore bark,
tender buds dipped in morning dew, fragrant and cool.
The little snail was very happy.

[P16] Summer fades into autumn, winter into spring.
Little snail has never forgotten the story his father told him.
When someone asks him, “Why is your house so small?”
He will tell this story—
The biggest house in the world.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《世界上最大的房子》的封面页，展示了书名、作者、译者及出版社信息，画面下方有六只蜗牛在草地上爬行。
[P2] 本页描绘了一群蜗牛栖息在一颗鲜嫩的卷心菜上，它们背着自己的壳，缓慢地在叶片间爬行，寻找最柔嫩的地方啃食。
[P3] 本页描绘了小蜗牛向爸爸表达想拥有世界上最大房子的愿望，爸爸认为这个想法愚蠢，并告诉他有些东西小一点更好，随后为他讲述了一个关于小蜗牛和房子的故事。
[P4] 小蜗牛不听劝告，躲在卷心菜叶的阴影里，通过不断尝试，终于找到了让自己的房子长大的方法。
[P5] 小蜗牛的房子越长越大，卷心菜上的其他蜗牛们纷纷称赞它为世界上最大的房子。
[P6] 小蜗牛持续努力，使自己的房子不断变大，最终变得像一个瓜一样大。
[P7] 小蜗牛通过不断尝试，学会了让自己的房子长出尖角，房子变得越来越奇特。
[P8] 小蜗牛通过不断努力，为自己的房子增添了鲜艳的色彩和美丽的图案，最终认为自己的房子是世界上最大最美的，感到自豪和快乐。
[P9] 一群蝴蝶飞过一只蜗牛巨大的、色彩斑斓的房子，误以为那是大教堂或马戏团，却不知道那其实是一只蜗牛的家。
[P10] 一群青蛙在去池塘的路上，被一只背着巨大、色彩斑斓的房子的小蜗牛所震撼，停下脚步并感叹其奇观。
[P11] 蜗牛们吃光了卷心菜的叶子，准备搬到另一棵卷心菜上，但那只小蜗牛因为房子太重而无法移动。
[P12] 小蜗牛因房子太重无法移动，留在原地后没有食物可吃，身体日渐虚弱变小，最终连房子也碎裂垮塌，什么都没剩下。
[P13] 故事结束后，小蜗牛几乎要哭了，但他随即想起自己的房子，并决定将来要让它保持小巧，以便长大后能自由移动。
[P14] 小蜗牛终于背上轻巧的房子，轻松愉快地出发去探索世界，沿途欣赏着微风中的叶子、闪烁的水晶、红点蘑菇、高耸的花茎、松果、鹅卵石和晨露中的花蕾，感到非常快乐。
[P15] 画面描绘了一片生机勃勃的森林地面，有蕨类植物、树桩、松果、鹅卵石和蘑菇，一只小蜗牛正从树根旁爬过，旁边散落着几颗色彩斑斓的蛋，其中一颗蛋上绘有彩色图案，暗示着小蜗牛的新家或新旅程的开始。
[P16] 本页是绘本的结尾部分，小蜗牛回忆起爸爸讲的故事，解释了自己房子为何如此之小。画面中两只小蜗牛在绿色的草地上爬行，象征着故事的结束与新的开始。右侧为图书的版权和出版信息。
